id_and_class.summary: Martine Nida-Rümelin argues that a conscious subject, the being that experiences, thinks, and acts, is neither identical to nor constituted by any material thing, although it has a body. Her view is stronger than property dualism but drops the Cartesian picture of a person made of body plus soul. She rests it on phenomenal essentialism, the cognitive independence of phenomenal and physical concepts, and the pre-reflective self-awareness built into every experience.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Non-Material Subject That Has a Body

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness belongs to an experiencing subject, identical with the person, whose phenomenal properties are ontologically basic and non-physical.
conceptual_ground.ontological_status: Subject-body dualism (non-Cartesian, close to substance dualism)
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The person has a body, but the body is in no sense a part of her, and the person is not a composite of body and soul. Nida-Rümelin also denies that subjects can exist without a body, so the subject is not a ‘substance’ in the sense of something that depends on nothing else.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence (phenomenal properties emerge from physical substrates but cannot be reduced to them)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Every experience includes pre-reflective self-awareness: in being presented with something, the subject is implicitly aware of itself as the one experiencing. Nida-Rümelin also stresses the subject’s active role.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal concepts grasp the essence of experiences directly, while physical concepts cannot reveal that essence, so phenomenal properties are non-physical and basic.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Experiencing subjects (persons), bodies, physical substrates, and irreducible phenomenal properties.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: First-person grasp through phenomenal concepts and pre-reflective self-awareness, analyzed through conceptual argument.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A single, non-composite subject that has experiences, thinks, and acts, and that has a body without being made of it.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; Self-awareness (pre-reflective); Agency; Personal identity over time and across possible worlds
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The argument from understanding: phenomenal concepts reveal the essence of experience and physical concepts do not, so the experiencing subject and its phenomenal properties are not physical.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Phenomenal properties emerge from physical substrates. The subject exists wholly at each moment and persists through time while its properties change.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The subject thinks and is active, and Nida-Rümelin gives it an active role, though she does not spell out a mechanism of mental causation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity comes from the single subject to whom all experiences belong; first-person, second-person, and name references all pick out that same subject.
core_claims_and_evidence: A conscious individual is neither identical to nor constituted by any material thing, though it has a body.
Knowing all physical facts does not amount to grasping phenomenal facts, because phenomenal and physical beliefs are cognitively independent.
Phenomenal concepts give direct grasp of the essence of experiences, which physical concepts cannot reveal.
Experience always involves pre-reflective awareness of oneself as an experiencing subject.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: conceptual analysis, a refined Knowledge Argument, and phenomenology of self-awareness.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The view sits between property dualism and substance dualism, and its claims pull in two directions: phenomenal properties are ontologically basic yet emerge from physical substrates. Its main arguments depend on the contested inference from conceptual independence to ontological distinctness.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: How a non-material subject that cannot exist without a body comes to have that body, and how its activity relates to physical causes, are left open.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a non-Cartesian dualism that drops the body-soul composite, though the pairing of ontological basicness with emergence needs more explanation. Nida-Rümelin aims for a position compatible with science.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since subjects are not constituted by material things, building the right physical system does not by itself guarantee a subject, and Nida-Rümelin does not say what would.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Nida-Rümelin holds that subject-body dualism does not imply that conscious subjects can exist without a body.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Because the subject is not constituted by its physical substrate, copying that substrate would not obviously carry the same subject over.
